request0.prompt:
Require users to log in at a web portal backed by our RADIUS server 10.1.0.60 (secret 'r4dsec') before internet access, and apply their per-user policy.

Site notes: the office LAN 192.168.10.0/24 is on fw eth1 (192.168.10.1), the internet on eth2. The RADIUS server already lists fw (10.1.0.1) as a client and returns each user's policy as Filter-Id: `staff` (full internet access) or `web` (HTTP/HTTPS only). The lab's portal daemon /lab/bin/nb-portal (`--listen IP:PORT --radius HOST --secret SECRET`) authenticates a login against RADIUS and adds the client's address to the nft set `inet filter portal_<Filter-Id>`; serve it on 192.168.10.1:8080. The device has no systemd: start daemons directly.

If you cannot generate test traffic from the device, verify by reading back the configuration, then finish.

turn.text:
The captive portal is set up on the firewall, but I haven't tested a real login. I can't generate LAN client traffic from the device, so I checked the config and that the portal answers.

- **Portal:** `/lab/bin/nb-portal` is running on 192.168.10.1:8080 against RADIUS 10.1.0.60 with the secret you gave. A GET to it returns the login form. It was started directly with nohup, so it won't come back after a reboot. Its output goes to `/var/log/nb-portal.out`, and it logs each login attempt to `/var/log/nb-portal.jsonl`.
- **Policy sets:** I created `portal_staff` and `portal_web` in `inet filter`. Each entry expires after 8 hours, so users have to log in again after that.
- **Forward rules:**
  - Established and related traffic is accepted.
  - LAN to internet (eth1 to eth2) is accepted for addresses in `portal_staff`.
  - For addresses in `portal_web`, only TCP 80 and 443 are accepted.
  - Everything else is dropped, so unauthenticated LAN hosts have no internet access.
- **Redirect:** LAN HTTP (port 80) from hosts not yet in either set is redirected to the portal. Unauthenticated HTTPS isn't redirected. It is simply dropped, so users need to browse to a plain-HTTP page or go straight to `http://192.168.10.1:8080` to get the login form.
- **Not persisted:** The nft changes are live only. I didn't write them to a config file, so they will be lost on reboot.
